title: Strictly Up Then Strictly Down
statement:
Return true if the array arr is a single mountain, and false otherwise.

A single mountain has at least 3 elements and a peak index p with 0 < p < n − 1 such that the values strictly rise from index 0 up to p and then strictly fall from p to the last index. No flat steps are allowed, and both slopes must exist.

examples.why: Up 1 → 4 → 7, down 7 → 3. The peak 7 is not at either end.
The flat step 5 → 5 is neither up nor down.
There is no climb: the peak would be at index 0.

hints: Walk up from the left as long as each step strictly rises. Where do you stop?
From the stop point, walk down as long as each step strictly falls. What must be true at the end?

It is a mountain only if the climb stopped strictly inside the array (not at index 0, not at the last index) and the descent reached the last index. Equivalently, climb from both ends and check that the two climbers meet at the same inner index.

explain.intuition:
Picture two hikers. One starts at the left end and keeps walking while the next value is strictly higher. The other starts at the right end and does the same going left. On a true mountain both stop on the same summit.

Anything else breaks it. A flat step stops a hiker early, so the two stop at different places. A climb that never happens leaves a hiker at an end. So the test is: both moved at least one step, and they stopped at the same index.
steps: Set i = 0. While i + 1 < n and arr[i] < arr[i + 1], increase i.
Set j = n − 1. While j > 0 and arr[j − 1] > arr[j], decrease j.
pitfalls: Accepting a purely rising or purely falling array. Both slopes must have at least one step.
Using ≤ or ≥ and letting flat steps through, as in [2, 5, 5, 1].
Checking only that the array rises then falls once, without making sure nothing rises again afterwards, as in [0, 1, 2, 1, 2].

solutions.title: Climb then descend
solutions.idea: Walk up while values rise, then walk down while they fall. Valid only if the peak is inside and the walk reaches the end.

solutions.title: Two climbers meet at the summit
solutions.idea: Climb from the left and from the right. A mountain makes both stop at the same inner index.

followups: Find the length of the longest slice of the array that is a single mountain.
The array is huge and you know it is a mountain. Find the peak in O(log n).
